note: Adapted from Sjöstedt's (1900) original description of Termes cavithorax, originally in German; the alate was not seen and the species is known only from a single nymph; total-length measurements of the minor soldier could not be recovered because of OCR damage and are not given; bionomics and specimen records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Fully developed alates are not yet known. Judged from the nymph, the species resembles E. atrox in having a median notch on the anterior margin of the pronotum; the head of the present species is round and triangular, whereas that of E. atrox is nearly circular; the clypeus is oval, not very large and not strongly convex; the anterior angles of the pronotum are broadly rounded and slightly, not deeply, depressed. Workers and soldiers differ completely from those of E. atrox: as a member of the former genus Termes, the present species has two soldier and two worker forms, with body lengths of 3–4 mm and 2.5–4 mm respectively, whereas E. atrox has only one form.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: body length 4 mm; generally similar to the minor soldier described below, but the apex of the mandibles is more strongly incurved and the antennae have only 14 segments, the short third segment being absent. Minor soldier: head pale yellow, nearly circular in dorsal view, the frontal margin forming a weak curve; mandibles slightly longer than half the head, blackish brown, pale at the base, slender and narrow, incurved at the apex; labrum large, triangular-ligulate, with a few hairs; antennae white, 15-segmented, the second segment only slightly shorter than the scape, the third segment the smallest, the remaining segments gradually larger towards the apex; pronotum rather large, about 2/3 the width of the head; anterior lobe rather small, contracted triangularly, with a distinct median notch; anterior angles of the posterior lobe slightly contracted, somewhat deflexed and rounded; posterior margin arcuate, slightly concave medially; upper surface of the posterior lobe with a broad shallow groove medially, the areas on either side of the groove raised; mesonotum about as wide as the pronotum, oval; metanotum of the same shape but distinctly wider, with a straighter posterior margin; hind tibia only slightly longer than the femur; apical tarsal segment as long as all the other segments together; body white, hairs rather long and sparse.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: head pale yellow, rounded-square in dorsal view, the sides rather straight, the occiput forming a very flat arc; the anterior angles below the antennal fossae almost squarely rounded; clypeus small, oval, with a triangular white area behind it, a distinct brown spot on each side, the white area bounded laterally by white lines that meet at an acute angle at the middle of the head and continue posteriorly as a similar line; first two mandibular teeth almost equal in size; antennae 15-segmented, entirely white, the scape not much longer than the second segment, the third segment the smallest, the following segments progressively larger and rounded outwards; anterior margin of the pronotum with a distinct median notch; anterior lobe slightly longer than the posterior lobe but narrower and slightly triangular; posterior margin arcuate, almost or quite without a median concavity; mesonotum as wide as the pronotum, oval; metanotum similar in shape to the mesonotum but wider; apical tarsal segment as long as the remaining segments together; hind tibia only slightly longer than the femur; body white, hairs rather long and sparse. Minor worker: distinctly smaller, body length 2.3 mm.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: A nymph shows in several respects the appearance of the alate: wing pads rather long, reaching the apex of the fifth abdominal segment; head short and round, triangular; clypeus oval, not very large, truncate anteriorly; first two mandibular teeth equal in length; antennae 17-segmented, the second segment rather large and distinctly broadened towards the apex, the third segment very small; pronotum semicircular, anterior angles broad and rounded, anterior margin short and reflexed, with a distinct median notch, posterior margin concave medially; body length 8 mm. The 17-segmented antennae and the notch on the anterior margin of the pronotum are the most characteristic features.
